jobs.title: Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**Environmental Scientist**

**Location:** Rancho Cordova, California (Office-Based / On-Site / Travel Required)

**About Us** Wilson Construction Company is a premier utility contractor specializing in complex electrical transmission and distribution line construction across the United States. Join Wilson’s Environmental Services team and help build electric utility infrastructure across California. The role is based in Rancho Cordova and supports our California offices and regional project sites.

**Role Overview** Based out of our Rancho Cordova, California office, the Environmental Scientist will work directly with construction crews and project managers to turn permit conditions and mitigation commitments into field practices. You will be responsible for coordinating environmental permitting, construction compliance, and mitigation plans while collaborating closely with superintendents, project managers, clients, and vendors to plan upcoming work and resolve environmental issues.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Permitting & Compliance:** Coordinate environmental permitting and construction compliance for projects and support compliance at Northern California facilities.
* **Site Inspections & Reporting:** Inspect active construction sites for stormwater, erosion and sediment control, spill prevention, and sensitive resource protection. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.
* **Mitigation & Training:** Develop and implement mitigation plans and coordinate stormwater controls, restoration, revegetation, and environmental training as needed.
* **Stakeholder & Client Liaison:** Work with superintendents, project managers, clients, and vendors to plan upcoming work and resolve environmental issues.
* **Project & Cost Management:** Track bids and active projects, prepare environmental cost estimates, and manage environmental costs during construction.

  

**Qualifications & Requirements**

* **Experience Level:** Five or more years of relevant experience, including conducting and documenting environmental fieldwork. Preferred qualifications include environmental compliance experience on utility or other infrastructure construction projects; California construction stormwater experience, including Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and field controls; and experience applying requirements under CEQA, NEPA, the Clean Water Act, endangered species laws, or Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act.
* **Education & Credentials:** Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, geology, natural resources, biology, or a related field. QSP or QSD certification is preferred.
* **Technical & Software Skills:** Proficiency with Microsoft Office.
* **Core Competencies:** Ability to write clear field reports, communicate requirements to field and office teams, and organize inspection and compliance records.
* **Location & Licensing Requirements:** Based in Rancho Cordova. Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to project sites. This role includes outdoor inspections and walking extended distances at active construction sites. Some assignments require extended stays away from Rancho Cordova.

  

**What We Offer**

* **Competitive Compensation:** Competitive salary.
* **Comprehensive Benefits Package:** 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision — for you and your qualified spouse and dependents.
* **Retirement & Paid Time Off:** 401(k) plan with company match, paid time off (PTO), paid vacation, and holiday pay.
* **Career Growth:** Professional development, specialized training, and career advancement opportunities within a national industry leader.

  

*Wilson Construction Co. is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.*

*We participate in E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility to work in the United States in compliance with federal law.*

*As a smoke and drug-free workplace, successful candidates must pass post-offer and random drug screenings, which include marijuana testing.*

  

**How to Apply** To apply, please submit your cover letter & resume via our website through the Opportunities page: www.wilsonconst.com.

* Spring 2027: January 15, 2027 – May 26, 2027

* Demonstrated commitment to working effectively with faculty, staff and students from diverse ethnic, cultural and socioeconomic backgrounds.

* Completion of a bachelor's degree in geology, environmental science, or related field, or equivalent coursework.

* Good oral and written communication skills.

* Evidence of satisfactory achievement in previous academic work, especially in the subject matter to be covered by the TA.

### **Job Description and Duties**

**ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENTIST (PERMANENT INTERMITTENT) – DIVISION OF BOATING AND WATERWAYS / AQUATIC INVASIVE SPECIES / NATURAL RESOURCES HEADQUARTERS**

  
  

The reporting location for this position is Division of Boating and Waterways located at 715 P Street at the Natural Resources Agency Headquarters in downtown Sacramento with an on-site cafe, local eateries and fitness center, public transit including suburban bus lines, Amtrak, transit incentives, public parking, bike lockers, and more. This position will report under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory).
  
  
Would you like to be part of a team charged with collaborating and cooperating to control invasive aquatic plants in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta? If you are, look no further than the Division of Boating and Waterways (DBW). As part of the California Natural Resources Agency and the Department of Parks and Recreation, DBW is a self-funded division dedicated to bringing together a body of knowledge as the state's expert in recreational boating-related matters, including public access, safety and education, marine law enforcement, and consumer and environmental protection. DBW's Aquatic Invasive Plant Control Program (AIPCP) strives to ensure that invasive aquatic plants in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta are managed to reduce the threat to economy, public health, and economy. We offer a progressive and family-friendly, cooperative work environment that values innovative thinking, collaborative approaches, enthusiasm for learning and continued job growth.
  
  
DBW's Aquatic Invasive Plant Control Program is recruiting an Environmental Scientist. Please see the Duty Statement for more information. Experience in natural resource management, hydrology, and field surveys desired.

jobs.description:
**Summary**
-----------

The ideal candidate is an expert in environmental and historic preservation (EHP) compliance with proven supervisory experience managing complex regional programs, serving as a national technical authority, and advising senior/high-ranking officials on EHP policy and compliance. The successful candidate will have experience exercising seasoned judgment and serving as a technical authority advising senior agency officials, regional leadership, and external partners.

Learn more about this agency

  

**This job is open to**
-----------------------

### **The public**

U.S. Citizens, Nationals or those who owe allegiance to the U.S.

### **Clarification from the agency**

This position is announced under FEMA's Excepted Service, Stafford Act Hiring Authority for a full-time Cadre of On-Call Response/Recovery Employee (CORE) appointment. After three years of continuous service, CORE employees earn competitive eligibility to apply for permanent full-time positions at FEMA. Veterans Preference does not apply to the CORE selection process.

  

**Duties**
----------

**What will I do in this position if hired?**

In this Supervisory Environmental Protection Specialist position, you will serve as a Supervisory Environmental Protection Specialist IC-0028-13, in FEMA's Region 9, providing supervisory oversight and coordinating Federal environmental planning and historic preservation (EHP) activities. Typical assignments include:.
  
  
Typical assignments include:

* Supervising a team of Environmental Protection Specialists, determining work priorities, and establishing short- and long-term project schedules.
* Serving as the regional technical authority, ensuring that all FEMA-funded activities comply with Federal regulations, Executive Orders, and laws such as the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA), the National Historic Preservation Act (NHPA), and the Endangered Species Act (ESA).
* Reviewing and approving complex, high-consequence environmental and historic preservation documents, including Environmental Assessments (EAs) and formal consultation records.
* Leading high-level negotiations and consultations with Federal, State, local, and Tribal partners (such as State Historic Preservation Offices and regulatory agencies) to resolve complex, controversial environmental compliance issues.
* Advising senior regional leadership, Congressional stakeholders, and program managers on critical, sensitive environmental policies and disaster-specific compliance strategies.
* Managing personnel deployments to disaster field locations and Joint Field Offices (JFOs) to provide on-site technical compliance support.

**What else do I need to know?**

**At FEMA, our mission is to help people before, during and after disasters, and every employee at FEMA has a role in emergency management.** Every FEMA employee has regular and recurring emergency management responsibilities, though not every position requires routine deployment to disaster sites. All positions are subject to recall around the clock for emergency management operations, which may require irregular work hours, work at locations other than the official duty station, and may include duties other than those specified in the employee's official position description. Travel requirements in support of emergency operations may be extensive in nature (weeks to months), with little advance notice, and may require employees to relocate to emergency sites with physically austere and operationally challenging conditions.

**This announcement is for a position as a CORE (Cadre of On-Call Response/Recovery Employee).** CORE employees are full-time employees hired to directly support the response and recovery efforts related to disasters. Employees are hired under the Robert T. Stafford Act and are excluded from the provisions of title 5, United States Code, governing jobs in the competitive service. They can be hired under a streamlined process instead of a competitive process. After three years of continuous service, Stafford Act employees may be granted competitive eligibility to apply for permanent full-time positions at FEMA.

  

**Requirements**
----------------

### **Conditions of employment**

To ensure the accomplishment of our mission, DHS requires every employee to be reliable and trustworthy. To meet those standards, all selected applicants must undergo, successfully pass, and maintain a background investigation for **Public Trust / High Ris**k as a condition of placement into this position. This may include a credit check after initial job qualifications are determined, a review of financial issues, such as delinquency in the payment of debts, child support and/or tax obligations, as well as certain criminal offenses and illegal use or possession of drugs (please visit: Mythbuster on Federal Hiring Policies for additional information). *For more information on background investigations for Federal jobs, please visit* OPM Investigations.
  
  
The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C, Non-career SES or Presidential Appointee employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the Human Resources Office.

**Conditions of Employment:**

* You must be a U.S. citizen to apply for this position.
* You must successfully pass a background investigation.
* Selective Service registration required.
* You must be able to obtain and maintain a Government credit card.
* You must be able to deploy with little or no advance notice to anywhere in the United States and its territories for an extended period of time.
* Please review the Additional Information section for additional key requirements.

### **Qualifications**

**All qualifications and eligibility requirements must be met by the closing date of the announcement.**

jobs.title: Safety & Environmental Specialist
jobs.description:
**THE JOB**

Tidewater Barge Lines is looking for a QHSSE Specialist to join our team to support our shipyard and environmental services teams! In this role, you will support the Company’s Quality, Health, Safety, Security, and Environmental programs by ensuring regulatory compliance, managing risk, and promoting a strong safety culture across facilities and operations, with an emphasis on shipyard and environmental services operations. This role conducts audits, inspections, and investigations. You’ll lead trainings and perform industrial hygiene assessments while providing guidance on QHSSE policies, procedures, and best practices. The position partners with employees and management to drive continuous improvement in safety performance, compliance, operational excellence, and environmental stewardship.

***Position will remain open until sufficient applicants are received***

The QHSSE Specialist responsibilities span multiple areas:

* **Safety Leadership & Risk Management**

  + Promotes and supports safe, incident-free operations and demonstrates compliance with applicable safety management system policies, procedures, and expectations. While providing technical expertise in the anticipation, recognition, assessment, and mitigation of risk
  + Administers Behavior-Based Safety (BBS) programs for the Shipyard and Environmental Services operations, including data analysis, hazard and risk assessment, corrective actions, and employee engagement.
  + Conducts industrial hygiene assessments and exposure monitoring, including air quality, noise, chemical, and other occupational exposures. Maintains, calibrates, and supports the proper use of applicable monitoring and testing equipment.
  + Analyzes safety, incident, exposure, and environmental data to recommend improvements to policies, and procedures while leading incident investigations, root cause analyses, and the development, implementation, and follow-up of corrective and preventive action processes.

* **Regulatory Compliance & Environmental Stewardship**

  + Monitors and supports compliance with applicable federal, state, and local safety, environmental, occupational health, and security requirements, as well as company policies, standards, and industry best practices.
  + Maintains current knowledge of applicable QHSSE laws, regulations, standards, and industry best practices, and evaluates their impact on company operations.
  + Conducts inspections, audits, assessments, and other compliance-monitoring activities; identifies deficiencies, recommends corrective actions, and supports continuous improvement efforts.
  + Maintains accurate and timely regulatory and company-required records, documentation, and reports.
  + Provides field-level support to the Environmental Manager for environmental compliance activities, projects, inspections, and other environmental matters within assigned operational areas.
* **Training & Employee Engagement**

  + Administers QHSSE training programs, including training requirements, scheduling, recordkeeping, learning management system administration, compliance tracking, and execute QHSSE-related training and awareness programs.
  + Maintains an active field presence at Shipyard and Environmental Services work sites, including the facilitation of safety committee meetings to identify hazards, reinforce safe work practices, and support regulatory compliance.

* **Operational Support & Program Administration**

  + Utilize feedback to plan and coordinates QHSSE projects arising from safety committee activities, employee safety suggestions, audits, investigations, and regulatory requirements.
  + Provide safety equipment, personal protective equipment, supplies, monitoring equipment, and other QHSSE resources for assigned operational areas.
  + Supports company drug and alcohol testing programs by serving as a qualified/certified collector adhering to DOT company requirements.
  + Communicates significant compliance issues to appropriate leadership and track corrective actions through completion.

* **Field Operations & Site Support**

  + Travels to company facilities and vessels to conduct inspections, audits, investigations, training, compliance reviews, and other program support activities.
  + Partners with operational leaders, vessel crews, and shoreside employees to implement QHSSE initiatives and support continuous improvement.

**PAY & BENEFITS**

* Position hiring range: $80,000 – $90,000 (depending on experience and qualifications)
* Bonus Potential
* Healthcare benefits including medical, vision, dental, and prescriptions with low deductibles and copays. Company pays 91% of premiums for the employee and family
* Flexible Spending Account
* 401(k) with 6% company match
* 3% Profit Sharing Plan
* Sick and vacation accrued per paycheck
* Nine paid holidays and one floating holiday
* Educational Assistance Program

**THE CATCH**

* Associate or bachelor’s degree in environmental, health, safety and/or security or other related field of study, or an equivalent combination of relevant experience and education.
* One to three years’ experience with a focus on quality, health, safety, security, and environmental compliance required. Experience in industrial, marine, terminal, and/or shipyard setting preferred.
* Basic understanding and ability to interpret federal, state, and/or local safety and environmental codes, rules, regulations, and procedures.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to deliver safety and environmental training, collaborate effectively, resolve problems, influence change, and build productive relationships at all levels of the organization.
* Be available on an on-call basis nights, weekends, and holidays to help respond to emergency situations.
* Be able to travel regularly to company facilities and work sites, including shipyard, terminal, and other operational locations including Pasco, WA and Kent, WA.
* Use all required personal protective

new_jobs.description:
**Environmental Scientist**

**Location:** Rancho Cordova, California (Office-Based / On-Site / Travel Required)

**About Us** Wilson Construction Company is a premier utility contractor specializing in complex electrical transmission and distribution line construction across the United States. Join Wilson’s Environmental Services team and help build electric utility infrastructure across California. The role is based in Rancho Cordova and supports our California offices and regional project sites.

**Role Overview** Based out of our Rancho Cordova, California office, the Environmental Scientist will work directly with construction crews and project managers to turn permit conditions and mitigation commitments into field practices. You will be responsible for coordinating environmental permitting, construction compliance, and mitigation plans while collaborating closely with superintendents, project managers, clients, and vendors to plan upcoming work and resolve environmental issues.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Permitting & Compliance:** Coordinate environmental permitting and construction compliance for projects and support compliance at Northern California facilities.
* **Site Inspections & Reporting:** Inspect active construction sites for stormwater, erosion and sediment control, spill prevention, and sensitive resource protection. Document findings and track corrective actions to closure.
* **Mitigation & Training:** Develop and implement mitigation plans and coordinate stormwater controls, restoration, revegetation, and environmental training as needed.
* **Stakeholder & Client Liaison:** Work with superintendents, project managers, clients, and vendors to plan upcoming work and resolve environmental issues.
* **Project & Cost Management:** Track bids and active projects, prepare environmental cost estimates, and manage environmental costs during construction.

  

**Qualifications & Requirements**

* **Experience Level:** Five or more years of relevant experience, including conducting and documenting environmental fieldwork. Preferred qualifications include environmental compliance experience on utility or other infrastructure construction projects; California construction stormwater experience, including Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs) and field controls; and experience applying requirements under CEQA, NEPA, the Clean Water Act, endangered species laws, or Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act.
* **Education & Credentials:** Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, geology, natural resources, biology, or a related field. QSP or QSD certification is preferred.
* **Technical & Software Skills:** Proficiency with Microsoft Office.
* **Core Competencies:** Ability to write clear field reports, communicate requirements to field and office teams, and organize inspection and compliance records.
* **Location & Licensing Requirements:** Based in Rancho Cordova. Valid driver’s license and ability to travel to project sites. This role includes outdoor inspections and walking extended distances at active construction sites. Some assignments require extended stays away from Rancho Cordova.

  

**What We Offer**

* **Competitive Compensation:** Competitive salary.
* **Comprehensive Benefits Package:** 100% employer-paid medical, dental, and vision — for you and your qualified spouse and dependents.
* **Retirement & Paid Time Off:** 401(k) plan with company match, paid time off (PTO), paid vacation, and holiday pay.
* **Career Growth:** Professional development, specialized training, and career advancement opportunities within a national industry leader.

  

*Wilson Construction Co. is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.*

*We participate in E-Verify to confirm employment eligibility to work in the United States in compliance with federal law.*

*As a smoke and drug-free workplace, successful candidates must pass post-offer and random drug screenings, which include marijuana testing.*

  

**How to Apply** To apply, please submit your cover letter & resume via our website through the Opportunities page: www.wilsonconst.com.

U.S. Citizenship
